correctness.rationale: E=x⁴/4+y²/2 is proper and has exact Lie derivative E′=−εx⁶−y⁴<0 off the origin, so all forward orbits exist and tend to the unique global attractor. At a positive y-semiaxis crossing with energy e, scaling x=√2 e^(1/4)u, y=√(2e)v, s=e^(1/4)Δt gives u′=v−2ε e^(1/4)u³, v′=−2u³−2e^(3/4)v³. The limiting regular quartic oscillator u′=v,v′=−2u³ has period T₀=4I₀ and all positive-section returns transverse, I_r=¼ B((r+1)/4,½). Smooth dependence yields physical return time Δt(e)=4I₀ e^(−1/4)(1+O(e^(1/4))) and exact energy defect e_next−e=−32ε I₆ e^(5/4)+O(e^(3/2)); y⁴ contribution is higher order e^(7/4). Hence e_j^(−1/4)/j→8ε I₆, t_j/j²→16ε I₀I₆. Monotonic energy between crossings and e_{j+1}/e_j→1 transfer to all physical time: t²E(t)→I₀²/(16ε²I₆²), N(t)/√t→1/(4√(εI₀I₆)). Regular complete limiting rotations plus entry into small-energy region ensure infinitely many positive-section crossings for every nonzero initial condition. Turnwise maxima give limsup √t|x|=[2ε(I₆/I₀)]^(−1/2), not pointwise limit. Mathematical scaling and coefficients verified independently; finite numerical turns do not certify all-times or all-initial-data assertions.
